The underground tour will take you between three separate interlinked artillery fortresses in the forest - but there are many more bunkers just off the main road.

properties.name: Chráněná krajinná oblast Broumovsko
properties.description: Sandstone spires form a city of pinnacles in the Broumovsko Protected Landscape Area, including the Adršpach-Teplice Rocks, Broumovské stěny, and Teplické skály.

properties.name: Stachelberg (dělostřelecká tvrz)
properties.description: The interconnected bunkers of the Stachelburg Artillery Fort was part of the Czechoslovakia Border Fortifications intended to defend against Nazi invasion -  only for it to be handed over to the Nazis without a fight following the Munich Betrayal. This is the largest fortress in Czechia, and features hiking trails between even more bunkers.

properties.name: Čertovy hlavy
properties.description: It's Mt. Rushmore, except haunted and Czech. In the 1840s a Czech artist carved terrifying massive faces into the stone. The weathering has made the carvings appear even more discomforting.

properties.name: Chráněná krajinná oblast Český ráj
properties.description: Czech Paradise Protected Landscape Area is teeming with sandstone pinnacles and historical castles. This includes the Prachov Rocks, Příhrazské rocks, Hruboskalsko, and the Trosky castle ruins located on top of an extinct volcano.

properties.name: Chráněná krajinná oblast Labské pískovce
properties.description: That's right it's even more beautiful Czech mountains located in the Protected landscape area of Labská pískovec. This is the companion park to the much more popular Bohemian Switzerland National Park. The protected area notably includes the sandstone pillars of Tiské stěny, and the canyons of Kaňon Labe.

properties.name: Muzeum starých strojů a technologií
properties.description: The Museum of Old Machines and Technology is a former Czech textile mill stuffed with 40+ antique cars, 20+ motorcycles, tractors, and locomotives,

properties.name: Národní technické muzeum
properties.description: The Czech National Technical Museum is a sampler of all technologies the Czech have created. In this museum there are cars, trains, and airplanes manufactured in Czechia. Notable exhibits include Austria-Hungarian Emperor Franz Joseph's railcar, and antique vehicles by Tatra and Skoda. For more in depth museums for each of these technologies, consider the Lužná u Rakovníka Railway Museum (trains), Aircraft museum Kbely (planes), and Muzeum starých strojů a technologií (industrial equipment and cars).

properties.name: Armádní muzeum Žižkov
properties.description: Czechia historically was conquered a lot due to being a small nation stuck between the great powers of Europe - so they've done a lot of fighting. The  Žižkov army museum tells the story of the Czech armed forces from the independent Kingdoms of Bohemia and Moravia, to subjugation under the Hapsburg monarchy (and uprising against it during the Bohemian revolt) , to the fight for the Czechoslovak Republic following the collapse of Austria-Hungary, subjugation by the Nazis and Communists (and the revolt of the Prague Spring against communism), and finally modern independence.

properties.name: Národní park České Švýcarsko
properties.description: Czech Switerland National Park is an area full of sandstone arches, gorges, and pillars that line the cliffs of the Elbe mountains.

properties.name: Nationalpark Sächsische Schweiz
properties.description: Saxon Switzerland National Park is composed of rock pillars sticking out of the Elbe mountains. Notably, the Germans built the Bastei bridge through the pillars so you can admire them from the sky.

properties.name: Park vojaške zgodovine Pivka
properties.description: The Pivka Park of Military History is the largest military museum in Slovenia. The museum features a strange mix of United States, Soviet Union, and Yugoslavian military vehicles and airplanes. A unique feature is the Yugoslavian Navy Una-class special operations submarine Zeta on display in the middle of the museum. There's also a 40 minute hike to the WW2 era Italian Alpine Wall Fortifications.

properties.name: Železniški muzej Slovenskih železnic
properties.description: Come see rusty Yugoslavian locomotives and some that are in good condition! The Slovenian Railway Museum features locomotives and equipment from Slovenian History. This includes 60+ locomotives and 50+ vehicles from the Austro-Hungarian Empire, to Yugoslavia, to independence.

properties.name: Regijski park Škocjanske jame
properties.description: The Škocjan Caves Regional Park features a massive underground canyon running through the middle, as well as a near vertical gorge on the exterior. There's also all the stalactites and stalagmites one would expect.

properties.name: Dimnice (jama)
properties.description: Dimnice Cave features a spiral staircase down the vertical mouth of the cave that feels as if you are descending into Hades.

properties.name: Postojnska jama
properties.description: This is THE European cave. The Postojna Cave system is 15 miles of caves full of massive rooms that are so big they feel fake. There are rooms in the cave with space for 10,000+ people that are used as concert halls, towering pillars of stalactites and stalagmites, an underground post office, and electric trains haul tourists through the caverns so they can see all of it.

properties.name: Grad Predjama
properties.description: It's a renaissance castle built into a cave in a cliff.

properties.name: Triglavski narodni park
properties.street: Na logu v Trenti, 5232 Soča, Slovenia
properties.description: Triglav National park is Slovenia's only national park, and is centered around Mount Triglav in the Alps. Notable hikes include the Vintgar gorge, which features a series of wooden walkways to a waterfall.

properties.name: Eigiau Dam
properties.description: The Eigiau Dam failed in 1925, killing 16 people downstream. The dam now sits in ruins near Llyn Eigaiau.

properties.name: Trianon Múzeum
properties.street: Várpalota, Gróf Apponyi Albert liget 1, 8100 Hungary
properties.description: Hungary took the blame at the end of WW1 and was cut down to 1/3 of its pre-war area, with 31% of all Hungarians living outside of the new borders. The treaty has left such lasting resentment that the Trianon museum was opened to showcase the downsides of the treaty.

properties.name: Atomenergetikai Múzeum
properties.description: Come learn about the Hungarian nuclear industry - which is really just a Soviet built reactor. You can see a replica of the the reactor at this museum - but the real thing is just down the road at a secured facility.

properties.name: RepTár Szolnoki Repülőmúzeum
properties.description: This is the Hungarian Aviation Museum. Unfortunately, Hungary doesn't particularly have an aerospace industry, so all the aircraft here are Soviet made.

properties.name: Magyar Vasúttörténeti Park
properties.description: The Hungarian Railway History Park is the main railway museum in Hungary, featuring 100+ railway vehicles from 1870s Austria-Hungary, to Communist domination, to the present. Including the streamlined MAV 242, streamlined Arpad diesel railcar which looks like it inspired the tabletop game Warhammer, and a miniature garden railway which you can ride around on.

properties.name: Hungarian Parliament Building
properties.description: The Hungarian Parliament Building is the defining piece of Gothic Architecture - inside and outside. You will need to reserve a tour in advance.

properties.name: SMS Leitha (1871)
properties.street: Budapest, Id. Antall József rkp., 1055 Hungary
properties.description: The 1871 SMS Leitha was the first river monitor in Europe, it's also the last one afloat.

properties.name: Terror Háza Múzeum
properties.description: During communist rule, Hungary was brutally repressed by the State Protection Authority (ÁVH), attempts at reform were put down by military force during the Hungarian Revolution of 1956. The House of Terror is a memorial to fascist and communist rule and features ÁVH torture cells that tourists can go inside of.

properties.name: Halászbástya
properties.description: The Fisherman's Bastion fortress overlooks the city of Budapest from the west bank of the Danube. The Fortress was rebuilt as a Neo-Romanesque style castle in 1895.

properties.name: Közlekedési Múzeum
properties.description: The Hungarian Technical and Transportation museum shows off Hungarian transportation from carriages to railroads to cars to airplanes. Yes they have the cool streamlined Arpad trains that look straight out of Warhammer.

properties.name: Chráněná krajinná oblast Moravský kras
properties.description: The Moravian Karst Protected Landscape Area covers the gorges and caves of the Moravian Karst - including the famous Macocha Abyss.

properties.name: Dobrošov (dělostřelecká tvrz)
properties.description: Dobrošov Artillery Fortress was part of the Czechoslovak border fortifications designed to protect the country from invasion against Nazi Germany. However, despite promises to defend democratic Czechoslovakia, the United Kingdom and France instead decided to hand over all of the fortifications to the Nazis following the Munich Betrayal. The fortifications of N-D-S 72 Můstek and N-D-S 72 Můstek are kept in great condition, and there are many more bunkers along trails if you want a nice stroll through the Czech countryside. .

properties.name: N-S 82 Březinka
properties.description: N-S 82 Březinka was an infantry blockhouse part of the Czechoslovakian Border Fortifications that were meant to defend the country from Nazi invasion - and they would have if the British and French didn't instead decide to hand the country over to the Nazis. Březinka has been nearly entirely restored - and is in near pristine condition. Because it's part of a continuous line of fortifications, there are trails to even more bunkers and fortresses nearby.

properties.name: Deutsches Marinemuseum
properties.description: The German Naval Museum focuses on the history of the German Navy, and features 5 prominent warships: an East German Libelle class torpedo boat, the Cold War era Type 205 submarine U-10, a Lindau-class minehunter, a Gepard-class fast attack craft, and the Lütjens-class missile destroyer Mölders.

properties.name: Deutsches Schifffahrtsmuseum
properties.description: The German Maritime Museum tells the story of German maritime history - including the bits from 1914-1945. The museum features the WW2 era Type XXI submarine Wilhelm Bauer, the 1924 ocean tug Seefalke, the 1940 whaling ship Rau IX, the 1908 lightship Bürgermeister Abendroth, and some other submarines and hydrofoils inside the museum.

properties.name: Soviet submarine B-515
properties.description: Tour the 1976 Soviet Tango-class submarine B-515, recently renamed U-434. This is the nicest Soviet Submarine in Germany - the other one is much rustier.

properties.name: Historisch-Technisches Museum Peenemünde
properties.description: The Peenemünde Historical Technical Museum is set in an old power station and features the history of the development of modern ballistic rockets. For some reason there's also the Soviet 1963 Juliett-class nuclear ballistic missile submarine U-461 docked nearby, and the Tarantul-class corvette Hans Beilmer.

properties.name: Rostock Schifffahrtsmuseum
properties.description: The Rostock Shipbuilding and Shipping Museum possesses the 1958 East German cargo ship Dresden. See the might of East German shipping.

properties.name: Deutsches Technikmuseum
properties.description: Come see overly complex German technology at the German Museum of Technology. Featuring two railway roundhouses full of 40+ locomotives, 270+ cars, a railcar hall with 50+ municipal transport vehicles, and some planes.

properties.name: Cap San Diego
properties.description: Come see the 1961 museum ship MS Cap San Diego - the pinnacle of West German Shipbuilding before containerization took over the industry.

properties.name: KZ Neuengamme
properties.description: 42,000+ people were killed by the Nazis at Neuengamme Concentration Camp between 1938-and 1945. Those that did survive were put on death marches, or loaded into empty passenger ships that were later sunk. The victorious allies later used the concentration camp as a prison for Nazis, and later as a state prison, then juvenile detention center until 2003.

properties.name: Deutsches Erdölmuseum Wietze
properties.description: The Germans love overly complicated machinery, and overly complicated machinery needs oil to run. Come see how Germany extracted oil at the German Oil Museum. 80% of all German oil production came from the surroundings of this museum. The museum features a lot of really tall oil rigs from 1899-present.

properties.name: Hubschraubermuseum Bückeburg
properties.description: Germany developed the first practical helicopter in 1936, come see the FW 61 and 53+ other helicopters at the Bückeburg Helicopter Museum. The museum also features the first British production helicopter (Bristol 171-Mk. 52), the experimental helicopters of Gerard Georges de Vastey, and the replica of the first helicopter to ever achieve flight in 1907.

properties.name: Externsteine
properties.description: 40-metre sandstone rock pillars carved with religious imagery rise out of the Teutoberg Forest. There's staircases so you can climb to the very top of the spires.

properties.name: LVR-Archäologischer Park Xanten
properties.description: The Roman Empire made it all the way up to Germany, and this archaeological park delves into the remains of the Roman colony of Colonia Ulpia Traiana. The ruins feature a mini version of the Colosseum, a temple, and gatehouse. There's also replicas of Roman ships.

properties.name: Eisenbahnmuseum Bochum
properties.description: The Bochum Railway museum features 120+ rail vehicles from 1853-1976 . Unique exhibits include a maglev, and a railbus - it's literally just a bus with train wheels.

properties.name: Deutsches Bergbau-Museum Bochum
properties.description: The German Mining Museum Bochum is a mine - in the middle of a city. You can learn about German mining, and actually go into the mine itself - which was built explicitly for tourism.

properties.name: Flugausstellung Peter Junior
properties.description: The Peter Junior Air Show is a private air museum with 100+ aircraft, including a replica of the Concorde which has been made into a café. There's also various Soviet and British airliners. The aircraft have very little fencing protecting them, so you can go right up to most of them.

properties.name: Museum für Antike Schifffahrt
properties.description: Come see actual Roman ships! Five Roman ships were discovered near Mainz on the Rhine in 1981, the remains were put inside the Museum of Ancient Seafaring, and full sized replicas were built of each of the ships.

properties.name: Eisenbahnmuseum Darmstadt-Kranichstein
properties.description: The Darmstadt-Kranichstein Railway Museum features 200+ vehicles. It's not the most specialized Railway museum in Germany, but it is one of the biggest.

properties.name: Schloss Bruchsal
properties.description: Sure Castle Bruschal is the really pretty palace of the Prince-Bishopric of the Imperial City of Speyer, but it's also home of the Deutsches Musikautomaten-Museum (German Music Machine Museum) - featuring a replica of the RMS Titanic's organ, and the Municipal History Museum.

properties.name: Dornier Museum Friedrichshafen
properties.description: Dornier was a German aircraft manufacturer from 1914-1996, during their operation Dornier produced massive flying boats, and experimental aircraft. The vertical takeoff cargo aircraft the Do 31, and the flying boats Do24, N25, and some satellites are here at the museum.

properties.name: Schloss Nymphenburg
properties.description: It's Bavarian Versailles. The Nymphenburg Palace was the summer Palace of the King of Bavaria from 1663 until the dissolution of German nobility in 1918. As Bavaria was one of the largest and wealthiest German states, the palace is one of the largest and most opulent. The massive palace complex is filled with museums, including the Museum of Man and Nature, and the Marstallmuseum (carriage museum) featuring 40+ preposterously ornate carriages.

properties.name: KZ Dachau
properties.description: Dachau Concentration Camp was one of the first Nazi concentration camps, and 41,500+ people were killed here either through murder, neglect, or in experiments. After the war the camp was used to hold Nazi war criminals for trial.

properties.name: Kehlsteinhaus
properties.description: The Eagle's Next has a restaurant at the top of a mountain, beautiful trails and a striking view of the mountains and valleys surrounding it. There's a bus from the Dokumentationszentrum that will take you to the elevator if you don't want to do the 4-hour round trip hike.

properties.name: Dokumentationszentrum Reichsparteitagsgelände
properties.description: The Nazi Party Rally Grounds in Nuremburg now lay in ruins like their failed ideology. The Documentation Center on the grounds tells the story of the showmanship and consequences of National Socialism, as well as the Nuremburg Trials where those that committed crimes against humanity met their deserved end.

properties.name: KZ Flossenbürg
properties.description: The Flossenbürg concentration camp killed 30,000 people during the forced labor in the granite quarries and Messerschmitt factories. This is not a happy place.

properties.name: KZ Mittelbau-Dora
properties.description: Mittelbau-Dora concentration camp is where 20,000+ people were killed. The slaves at the camp were forced to dig tunnels for the production of V-1 flying bombs and V-2 rockets. The tunnels still stand so that the horror can be toured.

properties.name: Stasi-Bunker Lübschützer Teiche
properties.description: The oppressive Stasi (Ministry of State Security) built bunkers to continue their stranglehold over East German freedom in the event of nuclear war. See how the secret police intended to survive the apocalypse at the Stasi-bunker.

properties.name: Sächsisches Eisenbahnmuseum
properties.street: An d. Dresdner Bahnlinie 130c, 09131 Chemnitz, Germany
properties.description: The Saxon Railway Museum is two railway roundhouses filled with 77+ railway vehicles, including the aerodynamic VT 18.16.

properties.name: KZ Sachsenhausen
properties.description: Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp killed 10,000+ people just outside of Berlin. After the war, the Soviets NKVD used it as a gulag for 60,000+ people.

properties.name: KZ Ravensbrück
properties.description: Ravensbrück Concentration Camp was primarily for women, and 90,000+ of them were killed here in gas chambers, forced labor, death marches, murder, human experimentation, and deliberate neglect.

properties.name: U 995
properties.description: The only place in the world you can go to the beach and go on a U-boat. The WW2 era Type VIIC/41 submarine U-995 is now a museum on the beach in Laboe.

properties.name: U 11 (U-Boot, 1968)
properties.description: The U-Boo-Museum Fehmarn has the Cold War era Type 205 Submarine U-11 available for tour. This is the most modern submarine available for tour in Northern Germany.

properties.name: Internationales Feuerwehrmuseum Schwerin
properties.description: Ever wanted to know how Communist East Germany fought fires? The International Fire Department Museum Schwerin has 112+ mostly East German firefighting vehicles. There's also little fire department displays for various countries to show off their firefighting history - including England, Poland, Switzerland, Czechia, France, The Netherlands, Denmark, the Soviet Union, and Austria.

properties.name: Technik-Museum Pütnitz
properties.description: This is THE East German vehicle museum. You can drive Soviet vehicles here - including the big ones. The Pütnitz Technology Museum is stuffed into three former Soviet Air Force Hangars. It features East German vehicles in three separate halls:  a hall dedicated to Military Wheeled Vehicles, a hall of  Civil Vehicles, and a hall full of tracked military vehicles and aircraft.

properties.name: Otto-Lilienthal-Museum
properties.description: Inventing flight is really hard. Otto Lilienthal was the first person to make repeated documented glider flights that would inspire the Wright Brother's development of the first aircraft. The Otto Lilienthal Museum features replicas of all of Lilienthal's known designs.

properties.name: Nautineum Dänholm
properties.description: This maritime museum features underwater laboratories and research submarines, including the underwater laboratory Heligoland and the underwater station BAH1. They're basically underwater houses. The museum has been closed to the public since 2022 - but it will reopen eventually.

properties.name: Otus (U-Boot, 1963)
properties.description: The Cold War era Oberon-class submarine HMS Otus served in the Falklands and Gulf War, and is now a museum ship in Germany after being privately purchased.

properties.name: Oldtimer Museum Rügen
properties.description: The Oldtimer Museum is a few massive falls filled with trains, planes, and 80+ automobiles. Notably the museum features the streamlined Soviet locomotive SDC class P36, East German cars and their West German counterparts displayed side by side,and a museum dedicated to the National People's Army of East Germany .

properties.name: Miniera di Serbariu
properties.street: Grande, Miniera di Serbariu, 09013 Carbonia SU, Italy
properties.description: The 1937 Serbariu Coal Mine on Sardinia is now a museum that offers tours of the mine (reservations required). The surface of the mine is reflects design patterns of the 1930s, so the whole facility has an oddly art deco feel to it.

properties.name: Segesta
properties.street: Contrada Barbaro, SR, 22, 91013 Calatafimi TP, Italy
properties.description: Legends are that the city of Segesta was founded by Trojan refugees. The ruins of the city now lay on top of a mountain, with a well preserved ancient Greek temple and theater situated on the edge of the mountainside.

properties.name: Selinunte
properties.street: Piazzale Bovio Marconi, 91022 Marinella TP, Italy
properties.description: The ancient city of Selinute has the ruins of an entire ancient Greek city and eight temples - and one of them has been reconstructed. It's kind of like running around 8 mini Parthenons with a beach view.

properties.name: Valle dei Templi
properties.street: 92100 Agrigento, Free municipal consortium of Agrigento, Italy
properties.description: A series of 7 ancient Greek temples lines the ridge of Agrigento. The mostly intact Temple of Concordia and the Temple of Hera are the standout attractions

properties.name: Parco archeologico della Neapolis
properties.street: Via Luigi Bernabò Brea, 14, 96100 Siracusa SR, Italy
properties.description: Neapolis Archaelogical Park lays in the ruins of the Corinthian city of Syracuse - the primary rival of ancient Carthage. The ruins contain a massive Greek Theater and the remains of a city crisscrossed with caves - including the famous Ear of Dionysius.

properties.name: Parco dell'Etna
properties.street: Stazione Partenza Piazzale Funivia Etna Sud, 95030 Nicolosi CT, Italy
properties.description: Mount Etna is a 11,165ft snow covered active stratovolcano on the warm Mediterranean island of Sicily. By active - they mean active - this volcano erupts nearly every year. You can hike to the top of the ash covered volcanic hellscape or hit the ski slopes.

properties.name: Paestum
properties.street: Via Magna Graecia, 919, 84047 Capaccio Paestum SA, Italy
properties.description: The ruins of the ancient Greek city of Paestum contain three fairly intact temples, an amphitheater, swimming pool, and council chamber. The ancient Greeks here were later assimilated by the nearby Romans - but the architecture remains distinctly Greek.

properties.name: Pompeii
properties.street: 80045 Pompei, Metropolitan City of Naples, Italy
properties.description: The Roman city of Pompei was buried in scorching ash clouds by the 79AD volcanic eruption of Mount Vesuvius. As a result, the city was largely preserved, and gaps in the ash allowed for the creation of plaster casts of the inhabitants as they were when they died.

properties.name: Parco nazionale del Vesuvio
properties.street: Sentiero del Gran Cono, 80056 Ercolano NA, Italy
properties.description: Mount Vesuvius National Park is centered on the 4,203ft tall active stratovolcano Vesuvius. Historically, Vesuvius has erupted and destroyed the cities surrounding it -but that hasn't stopped 600,000 people from living right next to it. At the national park, you can hike around and up to the rim of the volcano and see the smoldering crater.

properties.name: Herculaneum
properties.description: The Roman luxury seaside resort of Herculaneum was buried under the pyroclastic flow of the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79AD. Due to being buried by pyroclastic materials, the ruins of the city are better preserved than at nearby Pompei - there's still paint on the buildings. However, unlike Pompei there's no horrifying plaster casts of the dead.

properties.name: Museo nazionale ferroviario di Pietrarsa
properties.description: This is THE Italian train museum - and it's one of the few railway museums on oceanfront property. The museum is located inside a former locomotive factory and features 50+ locomotives including: a replica of the first Italian locomotive (Bayard Locomotive), a cube shaped steam locomotive, some streamlined diesel railcars, and the carriage of the Italian King.

properties.name: Galleria Borbonica
properties.street: Vico del Grottone, 3, 80132 Napoli NA, Italy
properties.description: The Bourbon Tunnel is an escape tunnel from the Royal Palace of Naples to nearby military barracks. The tunnel was later used as a bomb shelter during WW2 and contains wreckage of cars from Fascist Italy.

properties.name: Reggia di Caserta
properties.street: Piazza Carlo di Borbone, 81100 Caserta CE, Italy
properties.description: It's Neapolitan Versailles. The Royal Palace of Caserta was built as the main residence for the Kingdom of Naples (later the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies) in 1774, and is a sprawling palace and garden complex complete with massive artificial waterfall.

properties.name: Grotte di Castellana
properties.street: Piazza Franco Anelli, 70013 Castellana Grotte BA, Italy
properties.description: The Castellana Caves are characterized by a dramatic opening in the roof of the cave shining bright light upon the green stalagmites in a massive alcove.
